_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

It's easier to support and develop Pylint for both Python 2 and 3 if we don't support 2.6. It was a maintenance burden for us. Nevertheless, it was EOL-ed this year, you shouldn't expect from us to support it forever. It's my fault though that we didn't advertise this properly in our ChangeLog and in our release notes, but Python 2.6 support will not come back (except maybe the problem from setup.py).

_Original comment by_ **BitBucket: [stephenhsu](http://bitbucket.org/stephenhsu), GitHub: @stephenhsu?**:

---

Hi, I've found a way to solve this for `Python 2.6`. 
- Using `pip`

When installing `pylint 1.4.0` using `pip` for `Python 2.6`, errors will occurr, just as you guys have met.
The downloaded files of `pylint 1.4.0` are located in `/tmp/pip-build-root/pylint/`. Replace the lines 123 and 124 of `"setup.py"` to those of [setup.py](https://bitbucket.org/logilab/pylint/src/9365b042c352ea6d2c692f87a71e92a8262fd065/setup.py?at=default).
And then run `pip install pylint`. 
- Using source code

If you download the `.tar.gz` file or git clone the source codes to your specified directory. Just apply the changes as above, then run `python setup.py install`.

I've opened an [issue](#410/pip-cannot-install-pylint-of-version-140) to ask them to update the latest codes to pypi.
